title.zh: 卷二百五十六 列傳第一百四十四 崔景榮 黃克纘 畢自嚴 李長庚 劉之鳳
title.en: Volume 256 Biographies 144: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, Li Zhanggeng, Liu Zhifeng
title.raw: 卷二百五十六 列傳第一百四十四 崔景榮 黃克纘 畢自嚴 李長庚 劉之鳳 Volume 256 Biographies 144: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, Li Zhanggeng, Liu Zhifeng

sentences.zh: 崔景榮黃克纘畢自嚴李長庚

translations.literal: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, Li Zhanggeng.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, and Li Zhanggeng.

translations.literal: Opening bracket for an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening bracket for an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （王誌道）〉

translations.literal: (Wang Zhidao), closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: (Wang Zhidao), closing bracket.

sentences.zh: 劉之鳳

translations.literal: Liu Zhifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhifeng.

sentences.zh: 崔景榮，字自強，長垣人。

translations.literal: Cui Jingrong, style name Ziqiang, was a native of Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jingrong, whose style name was Ziqiang, came from Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授平陽府推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed as an investigating censor in Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，劾東廠太監張鯨罪。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and impeached the offenses of the Eastern Depot eunuch Zhang Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he impeached Zhang Jin, a eunuch of the Eastern Depot, for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 巡按甘肅、湖廣、河南，最後按四川，積臺資十八年。

translations.literal: He toured and inspected Gansu, Huguang, and Henan, lastly Sichuan, accumulating eighteen years of censorial seniority.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as touring inspector in Gansu, Huguang, and Henan, and finally in Sichuan, accumulating eighteen years of seniority on the censorial benches.

sentences.zh: 播州亂，景榮監大帥遇劉綎、吳廣輩軍。

translations.literal: When the Bozhou rebellion broke out, Jingrong supervised the armies of the supreme commander alongside Liu Ting, Wu Guang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: During the Bozhou rebellion, Jingrong was attached to the supreme commander's army alongside generals such as Liu Ting and Wu Guang.

sentences.zh: 綎馳金帛至景榮家，為其父壽，景榮上疏劾之。

translations.literal: Ting sent gold and silks in haste to Jingrong's home as a birthday gift for his father; Jingrong memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ting had gold and silks rushed to Jingrong's home as a birthday gift for his father, whereupon Jingrong submitted a memorial impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 播州平，或請以播北畀安氏，景榮不可。

translations.literal: When Bozhou was pacified, some requested giving northern Bozhou to the An clan; Jingrong would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: After Bozhou was pacified, some proposed awarding northern Bozhou to the An clan, but Jingrong opposed it.

sentences.zh: 會總督李化龍憂去，景榮為請蠲蜀一歲租，恤上東五路，罷礦使。

translations.literal: When Governor-General Li Hualong left office on account of bereavement, Jingrong requested remitting Sichuan's tax for one year, relieving the Upper East Five Circuits, and abolishing the mining envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Li Hualong resigned to observe mourning, Jingrong petitioned to remit one year's land tax in Sichuan, provide relief to the Upper East Five Circuits, and abolish the mining tax envoys.

sentences.zh: 化龍疏敘監軍功，弗及景榮。

translations.literal: Hualong's memorial narrating achievements in supervising the army did not mention Jingrong.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial recounting the merits of supervising the campaign, Li Hualong made no mention of Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 已，晉太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was advanced to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 三年滿，擢右僉都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: When three years were complete, he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his three-year term, he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 銀定素驕，歲入掠。

translations.literal: Yinding had long been arrogant and raided inward every year.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol leader Yinding had long been overbearing and conducted annual raids into the frontier.

sentences.zh: 景榮親督戰破之，因議革導賊諸部賞，諸部懼，請與銀定絕。

translations.literal: Jingrong personally supervised battle and defeated him; he then proposed abolishing rewards to tribes that guided bandits; the tribes were afraid and requested breaking with Yinding.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong personally led the troops in battle and defeated him, then proposed abolishing the rewards paid to tribes that guided raiders. Alarmed, those tribes asked to sever ties with Yinding.

sentences.zh: 銀定既失導，亦叩關求市。

translations.literal: Yinding, having lost his guides, also knocked at the pass seeking trade.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of his tribal guides, Yinding also came to the frontier passes to seek trade.

sentences.zh: 寧夏歲市費不貲，景榮議省之。

translations.literal: Ningxia's annual market cost was not small; Jingrong proposed reducing it.
translations.idiomatic: The annual frontier markets in Ningxia cost an enormous sum, and Jingrong proposed cutting them back.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，僅一市而已。

translations.literal: During three years in office, there was only one market.
translations.idiomatic: In three years in office he held only a single market.

sentences.zh: 其後延鎮吉能等挾款求補市，卒勿許，歲省金錢十余萬。

translations.literal: Thereafter Yan town's Jining and others, holding funds, requested restoring the market; in the end it was not permitted, saving more than a hundred thousand in gold each year.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jining of Yan Prefecture and others came with funds seeking to restore the markets, but he never agreed, saving more than a hundred thousand taels of silver annually.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，入為兵部右侍郎，總京營戎政。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of War, in overall charge of metropolitan military administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Wanli he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of War with overall charge of metropolitan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，以疾辭去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he soon resigned owing to illness.

sentences.zh: 逾年，起宣府大同總督。

translations.literal: After a year he was raised up as Governor-General of Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as Governor-General of Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 召還，晉兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital, he was advanced to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 會遼、瀋失，熊廷弼、王化貞議不協，命廷臣議經、撫去留，景榮數為言官所論。

translations.literal: When Liaodong and Shenyang were lost, Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen's plans were not in accord; the court was ordered to debate retaining or removing the military governor and grand coordinator; Jingrong was several times attacked by censors.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong and Shenyang fell, Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen could not agree on strategy. The court ordered a debate on whether to retain or dismiss the military governor and the grand coordinator, and Jingrong came under repeated attack from the censorate.

sentences.zh: 御史方震孺請罷景榮，以孫承宗代之。

translations.literal: Censor Fang Zhenru requested dismissing Jingrong and replacing him with Sun Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fang Zhenru called for Jingrong's removal and his replacement by Sun Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited illness and withdrew to his home.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年十一月，特起為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tianqi he was specially raised as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tianqi he was specially summoned to serve as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 當是時，魏忠賢盜國柄，群小更相倚附，逐尚書趙南星。

translations.literal: At this time Wei Zhongxian usurped national power; lesser men relied on one another in turn and expelled Minister Zhao Nanxing.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wei Zhongxian had seized state power, his faction of petty men had banded together, and they had driven out Minister Zhao Nanxing.

sentences.zh: 即家起景榮，欲倚為助。

translations.literal: Jingrong was raised from his home post, intending to rely on him as support.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong was summoned from retirement in the hope that he could be enlisted as an ally.

sentences.zh: 比至，忠賢飾大宅以待，景榮不赴。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Zhongxian had furnished a great mansion to await him; Jingrong did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Zhongxian had prepared a lavish mansion for him, but Jingrong refused the invitation.

sentences.zh: 錦衣帥田爾耕來謁，又辭不見。

translations.literal: Commander of the Brocade Guard Tian Ergeng came to pay a visit; again he declined and did not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ergeng, commander of the Brocade Guard, came to call on him, but Jingrong again declined to see him.

sentences.zh: 帝幸太學，忠賢欲先一日聽祭酒講，議裁諸聽講大臣賜坐賜茶禮，又議減考選員額，汰京堂添註官。

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Imperial Academy; Zhongxian wished to listen to the Rector's lecture one day early, and proposed curtailing the seating and tea gifts for listening ministers, also reducing examination-selection quotas and eliminating supplemental capital office appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy, Zhongxian wanted to hear the Rector's lecture a day in advance and proposed cutting back the ceremonies of seating and tea for attending ministers. He also sought to reduce the quota for examination selections and to purge supplemental appointments to capital offices.

sentences.zh: 景榮皆力持不行，浸忤忠賢指。

translations.literal: Jingrong forcefully held that none of these should be done, gradually offending Zhongxian's aim.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong firmly blocked every one of these measures, gradually running counter to Zhongxian's designs.

sentences.zh: 又移書魏廣微，勸其申救楊漣、左光鬥。

translations.literal: He also wrote to Wei Guangwei urging him to plead to save Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Wei Guangwei urging him to intervene on behalf of Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou.

sentences.zh: 廣微不得已，為具揭。

translations.literal: Guangwei had no choice and drafted a memorial for him.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, Guangwei drew up a memorial on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 尋以景榮書為征，曰：「景榮教我也。

translations.literal: Soon taking Jingrong's letter as proof, [Zhongxian] said: Jingrong taught me.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhongxian cited Jingrong's letter as proof and said that Jingrong had put him up to it.

sentences.zh: 」於是御史倪文煥、門克新先後劾景榮陰護東林，媚奸邪而邀後福。

translations.literal: Thereupon censors Ni Wenhuan and Men Kexin successively impeached Jingrong for secretly shielding the Donglin, flattering wicked men while seeking later fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Ni Wenhuan and Men Kexin then impeached him in succession, accusing him of secretly protecting the Donglin faction, flattering villains, and seeking future reward.

sentences.zh: 得旨，削奪為民。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript was obtained; he was stripped of office and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his dismissal and reduction to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，復原職。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen changed the reign era, his original post was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen reign began, his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 四年卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died; Junior Grand Mentor was conferred posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Chongzhen and was posthumously ennobled as Junior Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 黃克纘，字紹夫，晉江人。

translations.literal: Huang Kezuan, style name Shaofu, was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kezuan, whose style name was Shaofu, was from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: Eighth-year Wanli jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 除壽州知州，入為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Shouzhou and entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed prefect of Shouzhou, he later entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 累官山東左布政使，就遷右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he became Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong, then was immediately transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of that province.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ranks to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong, he was soon promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of the province.

sentences.zh: 請停礦稅，論劾稅使陳增、馬堂，他惠政甚著。

translations.literal: He requested stopping the mining tax and memorialized to impeach tax envoys Chen Zeng and Ma Tang; his other benevolent policies were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to halt the mining tax and impeached the tax envoys Chen Zeng and Ma Tang; his other benevolent policies were widely noted.

sentences.zh: 屢以平盜功，加至兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Repeatedly for achievements in pacifying bandits, he was advanced to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly rewarded for suppressing bandits, he rose to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四十年，詔以故官參贊南京機務，為御史李若星、魏雲中所劾，還家候命。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, he was ordered to assist Nanjing military affairs in his former rank; censors Li Ruoxing and Wei Yunzhong impeached him, and he returned home awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was ordered to assist Nanjing military affairs at his former rank, but censors Li Ruoxing and Wei Yunzhong impeached him, and he returned home to await the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 居三年，始履任。

translations.literal: After three years at home, he at last took up his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at home for three years before he was finally allowed to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 四十四年冬，隆德殿災，上疏陳時政，語極痛切。

translations.literal: In the winter of the forty-fourth year, when Longde Hall burned, he submitted a memorial on current affairs, the language extremely poignant.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the forty-fourth year, after a fire at Longde Hall, he submitted a memorial on current affairs in language of exceptional urgency.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 召理京營戎政，改刑部尚書，預受兩朝顧命。

translations.literal: He was summoned to administer metropolitan military affairs, transferred to Minister of Justice, and received the dying injunctions of two reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to administer metropolitan military affairs, he was transferred to Minister of Justice and received the dying injunctions of two emperors.

sentences.zh: 李選侍將移宮，其內侍王永福、姚進忠等八人坐盜乾清宮珠寶下吏。

translations.literal: When Lady Li the Select Consort was about to move palaces, eight of her inner attendants including Wang Yongfu and Yao Jinzhong were charged with stealing jewels from the Palace of Heavenly Purity and handed to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Li the Select Consort was to move out of the palace, eight of her attendants, including Wang Yongfu and Yao Jinzhong, were charged with stealing jewels from the Palace of Heavenly Purity and handed over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 克纘擬二人辟，余俱末減。

translations.literal: Kezuan proposed execution for two men, and reduced sentences for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan proposed the death penalty for two of them and reduced sentences for the rest.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，命辟六人，余遣戍。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree and ordered six executed, the rest banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disagreed and ordered six executed, with the remainder banished to frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 克纘言：「姜升、鄭穩山、劉尚理不持一物，劉遜拾地上珠，還之選侍，而與永福、進忠同戮，輕重失倫。

translations.literal: Kezuan said: "Jiang Sheng, Zheng Wenshan, and Liu Shangli took not a single thing; Liu Xun picked up pearls from the ground and returned them to the Select Consort, yet they are executed together with Yongfu and Jinzhong—the severity and leniency are out of proportion."
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan said, "Jiang Sheng, Zheng Wenshan, and Liu Shangli took nothing at all. Liu Xun picked up pearls from the floor and returned them to the Select Consort, yet they are to be executed alongside Yongfu and Jinzhong—the punishments are grossly disproportionate."

sentences.zh: 況選侍篋中物，安知非先朝所賜？

translations.literal: Moreover, how can one know that objects in the Select Consort's casket were not gifts from the previous reign?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, who is to say that what was in the Select Consort's casket was not bestowed by the previous emperor?

sentences.zh: 」當是時，諸珰罪重，謀脫無自，惟請帝厚待選侍，則獄情自緩。

translations.literal: At this time the eunuchs' crimes were grave; they had no way to seek release except to ask the emperor to treat the Select Consort generously, then the case would naturally ease.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuchs' crimes were grave and they had no way to escape punishment except to urge the emperor to treat the Select Consort generously, in the hope that the case would then be eased.

sentences.zh: 於是流言四布，謂帝薄待先朝妃嬪，而克纘首入其言。

translations.literal: Thereupon rumors spread everywhere, saying the emperor treated the previous reign's consorts poorly, and Kezuan was first to advance this talk.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then spread everywhere that the emperor was treating the late emperor's consorts harshly, and Kezuan was said to have been the first to voice such views.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，責克纘偏聽，命如前旨。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, reproached Kezuan for partial listening, and ordered as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, rebuked Kezuan for partiality, and ordered the punishments carried out as originally commanded.

sentences.zh: 已，楊漣陳「移宮」始末。

translations.literal: Thereafter Yang Lian set forth the beginning and end of the Palace Shift affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Lian laid out the full story of the "Palace Shift" affair.

sentences.zh: 帝即宣諭廷臣，備述選侍淩虐聖母狀。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately announced to the court ministers, fully narrating how the Select Consort abused the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately addressed the court, recounting in detail how the Select Consort had mistreated the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「大小臣工，惟私李黨，責備朕躬。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ministers great and small favor only Lady Li's faction and reproach my person."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Officials high and low favor only Lady Li's faction and lay blame upon me."

sentences.zh: 」克纘皇恐上言：「禮，父母並尊。

translations.literal: Kezuan in terror submitted: "By ritual, father and mother are equally honored."
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan submitted in alarm, "By ritual propriety, father and mother are equally to be honored."

sentences.zh: 事有出於念母之誠，跡或涉於彰父之過，必委曲周全，渾然無跡，斯為大孝。

translations.literal: Matters may arise from sincerity in remembering one's mother, yet traces may touch upon exposing one's father's fault; one must be tactful and complete so that nothing shows—this is great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Actions may spring from sincere devotion to one's mother, yet they may seem to expose one's father's failings; true filial piety requires handling such matters with tact so that no trace of fault appears.

sentences.zh: 若謂黨庇李氏，責備聖躬，臣萬死不敢出。

translations.literal: If it is said that I factionally shield the Li clan and reproach the sacred person, your servant would not dare speak though he deserved ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: If I am accused of shielding Lady Li's faction and reproaching Your Majesty, I would not dare speak even on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 」御史焦源溥力駁其持論之謬，末言：「群豎持貲百萬，借安選侍為名，妄希脫罪，克纘墮其術而不覺。

translations.literal: Censor Jiao Yuanpu forcefully refuted the error of his position, finally saying: "The eunuchs hold a million in funds, borrowing the name of securing the Select Consort, vainly hoping to escape guilt; Kezuan has fallen into their scheme without realizing it."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jiao Yuanpu forcefully rebutted his reasoning and concluded, "The eunuchs hold a fortune in bribes and, under the pretext of securing the Select Consort's welfare, hope to escape punishment. Kezuan has fallen for their scheme without realizing it."

sentences.zh: 」克纘奏辨，因乞罷。

translations.literal: Kezuan memorialized in defense and thereupon requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan submitted a defense and asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 略言：「源溥謂在神宗時為元子者為忠，為福藩者非忠。

translations.literal: He summarized: "Yuanpu says that in the Shenzong era, serving the heir apparent was loyal, serving the Prince of Fu was not loyal."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in summary, "Yuanpu holds that under Emperor Shenzong, supporting the heir apparent was loyal while supporting the Prince of Fu was not."

sentences.zh: 臣敢廣之曰：神宗既保護先帝，授以大位，則為神考而全其貴妃，富貴其愛子者，尤忠之大也。

translations.literal: Your servant dares broaden it thus: since Shenzong already protected the late emperor and bestowed the great throne, then for the late Shenzong to preserve his honored consort and enrich his beloved son is loyalty in the highest degree.
translations.idiomatic: I would broaden his point: since Emperor Shenzong had protected the late emperor and invested him with the throne, to honor Shenzong's consort and provide for his beloved son is the highest form of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 又謂在先帝時為二後者為忠，為選侍者非忠。

translations.literal: He also says that in the late emperor's time, serving the two empresses was loyal, serving the Select Consort was not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He also holds that under the late emperor, supporting the two empresses was loyal while supporting the Select Consort was not.

sentences.zh: 臣亦廣之曰：聖母既正名定位，則光昭刑於之令德，勿虛傳宮幃之忿爭，尤忠之大也。

translations.literal: Your servant also broadens it thus: since the empress dowager has already been given correct name and position, then to glorify her exemplary virtue in the "Ode to the Mulberry" and not vainly spread palace quarrels is loyalty in the highest degree.
translations.idiomatic: I would likewise broaden his point: since the empress dowager has been properly installed in her rank, to honor her exemplary virtue and not spread idle tales of palace quarrels is the highest form of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 若如源溥言，必先帝不得正其始，聖母不得正其終，方可議斯獄耳。

translations.literal: If as Yuanpu says, only when the late emperor could not rectify his beginning and the empress dowager could not rectify her end could this case be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuanpu is right, this case could be debated only if the late emperor had failed at the outset and the empress dowager at the close—which is plainly not so.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝怒甚，責以輕肆無忌，不諳忠孝。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was very angry and reproached him for frivolous presumption without restraint and not understanding filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, the emperor was furious and rebuked Kezuan for presumptuous irreverence and failure to understand filial duty.

sentences.zh: 克纘皇恐引罪，大學士劉一燝等亦代為言，乃已。

translations.literal: Kezuan in terror accepted guilt; Grand Secretaries Liu Yijing and others also spoke on his behalf, and it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan accepted blame in alarm, and Grand Secretaries Liu Yijing and others interceded on his behalf until the matter subsided.

sentences.zh: 無何，給事中董承業、孫傑、毛士龍，御史潘雲翼、楊新期，南京御史王允成並劾克纘是非舛謬。

translations.literal: Before long, supervising secretaries Dong Chengye, Sun Jie, and Mao Shilong, censors Pan Yunyi and Yang Xinqi, and Nanjing censor Wang Yuncheng together impeached Kezuan for confused right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, supervising secretaries Dong Chengye, Sun Jie, and Mao Shilong, censors Pan Yunyi and Yang Xinqi, and Nanjing censor Wang Yuncheng jointly impeached Kezuan for confused judgment.

sentences.zh: 克纘不服，言曩不舉李三才，故為諸人所惡。

translations.literal: Kezuan would not accept it and said that because he had not earlier recommended Li Sancai, he was hated by many.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan protested, saying that because he had not recommended Li Sancai earlier, he was hated by his critics.

sentences.zh: 源溥復劾克纘借三才以傾言官。

translations.literal: Yuanpu again impeached Kezuan for using Sancai to overturn the censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanpu again impeached him, accusing him of using Li Sancai to undermine the censorate.

sentences.zh: 克纘奏辨，再乞休，帝不問。

translations.literal: Kezuan memorialized in defense and again requested retirement; the emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan defended himself and again asked to retire, but the emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年冬，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tianqi he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Tianqi he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋復以兵部尚書協理戎政。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Minister of War assisting in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Minister of War to assist in military administration.

sentences.zh: 廷臣議「紅丸」，克纘述進藥始末，力為方從哲辨。

translations.literal: The court debated the Red Pill affair; Kezuan narrated the beginning and end of administering the medicine and forcefully defended Fang Congzhe.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated the "Red Pill" affair, Kezuan recounted how the medicine had been administered and vigorously defended Fang Congzhe.

sentences.zh: 給事中薛文周詆其滅倫常，昵私交，昧大義。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Xue Wenzhou slandered him for extinguishing human relations, being intimate with private associates, and obscuring great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Xue Wenzhou accused him of subverting moral order, favoring private associates, and ignoring the larger public interest.

sentences.zh: 克纘憤，援《春秋》不書隱公、閔公之弒，力詆文周，且白選侍無毆聖母事。

translations.literal: Kezuan was angry, citing that the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record the assassinations of Duke Yin and Duke Min, forcefully attacking Wenzhou, and also declaring that the Select Consort had no affair of beating the empress dowager to death.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan, indignant, cited the *Spring and Autumn Annals'* refusal to record the assassinations of Duke Yin and Duke Min, attacked Wenzhou forcefully, and insisted that the Select Consort had never beaten the empress dowager to death.

sentences.zh: 給事中沈惟炳助文周復劾克纘。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Shen Weibing aided Wenzhou in again impeaching Kezuan.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Shen Weibing joined Wenzhou in impeaching Kezuan again.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝宣諭百官，明言選侍毆崩聖母。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had announced to the hundred officials, clearly stating that the Select Consort beat the empress dowager to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had announced to the entire bureaucracy that the Select Consort had beaten the empress dowager to death.

sentences.zh: 及惟炳疏上，得旨：「選侍向有觸忤，朕一時傳諭，不無過激。

translations.literal: When Weibing's memorial went up, a rescript was obtained: "The Select Consort had offenses of insolence; I for a moment transmitted the announcement, not without excess."
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Weibing's memorial was submitted, the emperor replied, "The Select Consort had indeed given offense, and my announcement at the time was not without excess."

sentences.zh: 追念皇考，豈能恝然？

translations.literal: Recalling my late father, how could I be indifferent?
translations.idiomatic: When I recall my late father, how can I remain indifferent to her welfare?

sentences.zh: 」於是外議紛紜，鹹言前此上諭，悉出王安矯托，而諸請安選侍者，益得藉為詞。

translations.literal: Thereupon outside opinion was in turmoil; all said the previous imperial announcements all came from Wang An's false pretense, and those who requested securing the Select Consort gained further words to borrow.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion then erupted, with many claiming that the earlier imperial announcements had all been forged by Wang An, while those who urged leniency toward the Select Consort gained fresh arguments.

sentences.zh: 蓋是時王安已死，魏忠賢方竊柄，故前後諭旨牴牾如此。

translations.literal: For at this time Wang An was already dead and Wei Zhongxian was just usurping power, hence the earlier and later edicts contradicted thus.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wang An was dead and Wei Zhongxian was seizing power, which explains why the earlier and later edicts contradicted each other so sharply.

sentences.zh: 克纘歷官中外，清強有執。

translations.literal: Kezuan served in office inside and outside the capital, upright, forceful, and principled.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan served both in the capital and in the provinces, distinguished by integrity, firmness, and principle.

sentences.zh: 持議與爭「三案」者異，攻擊紛起。

translations.literal: His held opinions differed from those contending over the Three Cases, and attacks arose in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: His views differed from those debating the "Three Cases," and attacks against him multiplied.

sentences.zh: 自是群小排東林，創《要典》，率推克纘為首功。

translations.literal: From this time petty men expelled the Donglin, created the *Essentials Canon*, and generally promoted Kezuan as chief merit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the faction of petty men drove out the Donglin, compiled the *Essentials Canon*, and generally hailed Kezuan as their leading champion.

sentences.zh: 時東林方盛，克纘移疾。

translations.literal: When the Donglin was flourishing, Kezuan cited illness.
translations.idiomatic: While the Donglin faction was at its height, Kezuan cited illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子太傅，乘傳歸。

translations.literal: He was ordered given the additional title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and returned home by post-horse relay.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and sent home by imperial relay.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，魏忠賢盡逐東林，召克纘為工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Wei Zhongxian expelled the Donglin entirely and summoned Kezuan as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, after Wei Zhongxian had driven out the Donglin entirely, Kezuan was recalled as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 視事數月，復移疾歸。

translations.literal: After several months in office, he again cited illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After only a few months in office he again cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 三殿成，加太子太師。

translations.literal: When the Three Halls were completed, he was given the additional title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Halls were completed, he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned back as Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 有劾之者，不就，卒於家。

translations.literal: There were those who impeached him; he did not take office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachment followed; he declined the appointment and died at home.

sentences.zh: 畢自嚴，字景曾，淄川人。

translations.literal: Bi Ziyan, courtesy name Jingceng, was a man of Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Ziyan, styled Jingceng, came from Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twentieth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 除松江推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor of Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 年少有才幹，征授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Young and talented, he was summoned and appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Still young but already capable, he was called to the capital and made a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 歷工部員外郎中，遷淮徐道參議。

translations.literal: He served as an outer and inner bureau director in the Ministry of Works, then was transferred to assistant administration commissioner of the Huai-Xu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through outer and inner bureau posts in the Ministry of Works, then became assistant administration commissioner on the Huai-Xu circuit.

sentences.zh: 內艱闋，分守冀寧。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, he was assigned divided defense of Ji-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning leave ended, he was put in charge of divided defense in the Ji-Ning area.

sentences.zh: 改河東副使，引疾去。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice commissioner of Hedong and, citing illness, departed.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Hedong, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 起洮岷兵備參政。

translations.literal: He was recalled as administration commissioner for Tao-Min frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as administration commissioner charged with Tao-Min frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 以按察使徙治榆林西路，進右布政使。

translations.literal: As surveillance commissioner he was moved to govern the West Route of Yulin and was promoted to right administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from surveillance commissioner, he took charge of the West Route of Yulin and advanced to right administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 泰昌時，召為太仆卿。

translations.literal: In the Taichang reign he was summoned as Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang reign he was called up as Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年四月，遼陽覆。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi, Liaoyang fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi, Liaoyang was lost.

sentences.zh: 廷議設天津巡撫，專飭海防，改自嚴右僉都御史以往。

translations.literal: The court debated establishing a grand coordinator at Tianjin devoted solely to tightening coastal defense, and Ziyan was changed to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent there.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided to create a Tianjin grand coordinator devoted to coastal defense, and Ziyan was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent to fill the post.

sentences.zh: 置水軍，繕戰艦，備戎器。

translations.literal: A naval force was established, warships were repaired, and weapons were readied.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a naval force, refitted warships, and stocked arms.

sentences.zh: 及熊廷弼建三方布置策，天津居其一，增設鎮海諸營，用戚繼光遺法，水軍先習陸戰，軍由是可用。

translations.literal: When Xiong Tingbi devised the strategy of deploying on three fronts, Tianjin was one of them; additional camps such as Zhenhai were set up, and Qi Jiguang's legacy method was used—naval troops first trained in land warfare—so the army became usable.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong Tingbi laid out his three-front deployment, Tianjin formed one corner of it; new camps such as Zhenhai were added, and following Qi Jiguang's old practice the sailors were drilled first in land fighting, until the force could actually be used.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢令錦衣千戶劉僑逮天津廢將，自嚴以無駕帖疏論之，報聞。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian ordered the Brocade Guard chiliarch Liu Qiao to arrest dismissed generals at Tianjin; Ziyan memorialized that there was no imperial warrant, and a report was acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian sent Brocade Guard chiliarch Liu Qiao to seize dismissed generals at Tianjin; Ziyan memorialized that no imperial warrant had been issued, and the court took note.

sentences.zh: 四方所募兵日逃亡，用自嚴言，攝其親屬補伍。

translations.literal: Troops recruited from the four directions fled daily; following Ziyan's proposal, their kin were seized to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Mercenaries raised across the realm deserted every day; on Ziyan's advice their families were detained to make up the shortfall in the rolls.

sentences.zh: 兵部主事來斯行有武略，自嚴請為監軍。

translations.literal: Lai Sihang, a principal secretary in the Ministry of War, had military talent, and Ziyan requested him as supervising general.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Sihang, a principal secretary in the Ministry of War, was skilled in military affairs, and Ziyan asked that he serve as supervising general.

sentences.zh: 山東白蓮妖賊起，令斯行率五千人往，功多。

translations.literal: White Lotus demon bandits rose in Shandong; he ordered Sihang to lead five thousand men thither, and the achievements were many.
translations.idiomatic: When White Lotus rebels broke out in Shandong, he sent Sihang at the head of five thousand men; the victories piled up.

sentences.zh: 初，萬歷四十六年，遼左用兵，議行登、萊海運。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the forty-sixth year of Wanli, when troops were used in eastern Liaodong, it was debated to run sea transport from Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the forty-sixth year of Wanli, as the eastern Liaodong campaign began, the court debated opening sea transport from Dengzhou and Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，特設戶部侍郎一人，兼右僉都御史，出督遼餉，語詳《李長庚傳》。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially appointed, also holding the title Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to go out and supervise Liaodong provisions—the details are given in the *Biography of Li Zhanggeng*.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially created, concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to supervise Liaodong supplies in the field; the account is given in the *Biography of Li Zhanggeng*.

sentences.zh: 及是，長庚遷，乃命自嚴代。

translations.literal: At this time Zhanggeng was transferred, and Ziyan was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhanggeng moved on, Ziyan was appointed in his stead.

sentences.zh: 敘前平賊功，進右都御史兼戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In recognition of his earlier merit in pacifying bandits, he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Left Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier success against the rebels was rewarded with promotion to Right Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Left Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時議省天津巡撫，令督餉侍郎兼領其事，即以委自嚴。

translations.literal: The court then debated abolishing the Tianjin grand coordinator and letting the vice minister supervising provisions also oversee that duty; the task was entrusted to Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: The court also debated abolishing the Tianjin grand coordinator and folding the post into the supply supervisor's portfolio; Ziyan was given both responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 又議討朝鮮，自嚴言不可遽討，當俟請貢輸誠，東征效力，徐許其封耳。

translations.literal: There was further debate on attacking Korea; Ziyan said it could not be attacked hastily—one should wait until they begged to offer tribute and showed sincerity, then let them serve the eastern campaign, and only then slowly grant investiture.
translations.idiomatic: When an attack on Korea was proposed, Ziyan argued that no sudden strike should be made: wait until they sought investiture and proved their loyalty, let them aid the eastern expedition, and only then grant their title in due course.

sentences.zh: 京師數地震，因言內批宜慎，恩澤宜節，人才宜惜，內操宜罷，語甚切直。

translations.literal: The capital suffered repeated earthquakes; he therefore said inner rescripts should be cautious, favors should be restrained, talent should be cherished, and inner-court drill troops should be abolished—his words were very blunt.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated earthquakes in the capital he urged caution in inner-court rescripts, restraint in imperial largesse, care for capable men, and an end to palace drill regiments—memorial after memorial, blunt to the bone.

sentences.zh: 自嚴在事數年，綜核撙節，公私賴之。

translations.literal: Ziyan held office several years, examining accounts and practicing frugality, and public and private affairs relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: For several years in office Ziyan audited accounts and enforced thrift, and both the state and his colleagues leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 五年，以右都御史掌南京都察院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he took charge of the Nanjing Censorate as Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Right Censor-in-Chief and placed over the Nanjing Censorate.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，就改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he was immediately changed to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, he was shifted at once to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 忠賢議鬻南太仆牧馬草場，助殿工。

translations.literal: Zhongxian proposed selling the Nanjing Imperial Stud's pasturelands to fund palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian proposed selling the Southern Capital stud farms to pay for palace works.

sentences.zh: 自嚴持不可，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: Ziyan held that it could not be done and, citing illness, returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan refused, then pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 自嚴以度支大絀，請核逋賦，督屯田，嚴考成，汰冗卒，停薊、密、昌、永四鎮新增鹽菜銀二十二萬，俱報可。

translations.literal: Ziyan, because revenue was greatly strained, requested verification of arrears, supervision of garrison farms, strict performance review, elimination of redundant soldiers, and suspension of the newly added salt-and-provisions silver of two hundred twenty thousand taels for the four garrisons of Ji, Mi, Chang, and Yong—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: With the treasury in dire straits, Ziyan asked to audit arrears, tighten garrison farming, enforce performance standards, cut useless troops, and halt the new salt-and-rations payments of 220,000 taels at Ji, Mi, Chang, and Yong; the emperor approved every item.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，疏言：「諸邊年例，自遼餉外，為銀三百二十七萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year he memorialized: "The annual quotas of the frontiers, apart from Liaodong supplies, amount to 3,278,000-odd taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year he submitted a memorial: "Apart from Liaodong funds, the frontier's annual quotas total 3,278,000-odd taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 今薊、密諸鎮節省三十三萬，尚應二百九十四萬八千。

translations.literal: Now the Ji and Mi garrisons have saved three hundred thirty thousand, yet two hundred ninety-four thousand eight hundred should still be required.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Mi have already saved 330,000 taels, yet 294,800 taels are still owed.

sentences.zh: 統計京邊歲入之數，田賦百六十九萬二千，鹽課百一十萬三千，關稅十六萬一千，雜稅十萬三千，事例約二十萬，凡三百二十六萬五千有奇。

translations.literal: Tallying the capital and frontier annual receipts: land tax 1,692,000, salt levy 1,103,000, transit duties 161,000, miscellaneous taxes 103,000, and precedent purchases about 200,000—in all 3,265,000-odd.
translations.idiomatic: Count all receipts for the capital and the frontiers: land tax 1,692,000; salt 1,103,000; transit duties 161,000; miscellaneous levies 103,000; precedent purchases about 200,000—3,265,000-odd in all.

sentences.zh: 而逋負相沿，所入不滿二百萬，即盡充邊餉，尚無贏余。

translations.literal: Yet arrears run on in succession, and receipts do not reach two million; even if all were devoted to frontier pay, there would still be no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet arrears pile up year after year, and actual intake falls short of two million taels; pour every coin into frontier pay and there is still nothing left over.

sentences.zh: 乃京支雜項八十四萬，遼東提塘三十余萬，薊、遼撫賞十四萬，遼東舊餉改新餉二十萬，出浮於入，已一百十三萬六千。

translations.literal: Then capital disbursements in miscellaneous items are eight hundred forty thousand, Liaodong courier stations more than three hundred thousand, Ji-Liao reward silver one hundred forty thousand, and the old Liaodong pay converted to new pay two hundred thousand—expenditure already exceeds income by 1,136,000.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the capital spends 840,000 taels on miscellaneous items; Liaodong courier posts take more than 300,000; Ji-Liao reward funds 140,000; and converting old Liaodong stipends to the new scale costs 200,000—expenditure already outruns income by 1,136,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 況內供召買，宣、大撫賞，及一切不時之需，又有出常額外者。

translations.literal: Moreover inner-court requisitions, Xuan-Da reward funds, and every unscheduled need draw still more beyond the regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that come inner-court purchases, Xuan-Da reward payments, and every emergency levy beyond the regular budget.

sentences.zh: 乞敕下廷臣，各陳所見。

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty command the court ministers each to set forth his views.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to order every minister at court to lay his views before the throne.

sentences.zh: 」於是廷臣爭效計畫。

translations.literal: "Thereupon court ministers vied to offer plans.
translations.idiomatic: "Courtiers then rushed forward with plans of their own.

sentences.zh: 自嚴擇其可者，先列上十二事，曰增鹽引，議鼓鑄，括雜稅，核隱田，稅寺產，核牙行，停修倉廒，止葺公署，南馬協濟，崇文鋪稅，京運撥兌，板木折價。

translations.literal: Ziyan chose what was feasible and first submitted twelve measures: increase salt certificates, discuss coin casting, comb miscellaneous taxes, verify concealed fields, tax monastery property, verify broker houses, stop repairing granaries, halt repairing government offices, southern horse mutual aid, Chongwen market tax, capital transport allocation exchange, and timber discounted to cash.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan sifted the proposals and first sent up twelve measures—increase salt certificates, mint new coin, sweep miscellaneous levies, audit hidden land, tax monastic estates, inspect broker houses, stop granary repairs, halt office renovations, mutual aid for southern horses, Chongwen market dues, reallocate capital grain transport, and discount timber to cash.

sentences.zh: 已，復列上十二事，曰增關稅，捐公費，鬻生祠，酌市稅，汰冗役，核虛冒，加抵贖，班軍折銀，吏胥納班，河濱灘蕩，京東水田，殿工冠帶。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted twelve more: increase transit duties, donate public expenses, sell living shrines, adjust market taxes, eliminate redundant laborers, verify false claims, increase commutation fines, convert garrison troops to silver, clerks pay roster fees, riverbank tidal flats, eastern capital paddy fields, and palace works honorary titles.
translations.idiomatic: He then added twelve more—raise transit duties, cut public waste, sell "living shrines," adjust market taxes, purge redundant staff, expose false claims, raise redemption fines, pay garrison troops in silver, make clerks buy roster slots, lease river flats, develop eastern-capital paddies, and sell honorary titles to fund the palaces.

sentences.zh: 帝悉允行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved them all for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every item.

sentences.zh: 詔輯《賦役全書》。

translations.literal: An edict ordered compilation of the *Complete Book of Taxes and Corvée*.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the compilation of the *Complete Book of Taxes and Corvée*.

sentences.zh: 自嚴言：「《全書》之作，自行一條鞭始，距今已四十五年。

translations.literal: Ziyan said: "The making of the *Complete Book* began with the single-whip reform; from then until now forty-five years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan wrote: "The *Complete Book* dates from the single-whip reform; forty-five years have passed since then.

sentences.zh: 有一事而此多彼少者，其弊為混派；

translations.literal: Where one matter is assessed heavily here and lightly there, the abuse is mixed apportionment;
translations.idiomatic: When one levy is heavy in one county and light in another, the abuse is mixed apportionment;

sentences.zh: 有司聽奸吏暗灑瓜分，其弊為花派。

translations.literal: where clerks heed corrupt underlings who secretly sprinkle and divide assessments, the abuse is phantom apportionment.
translations.idiomatic: when clerks let corrupt runners secretly split and reassign quotas, the abuse is phantom apportionment.

sentences.zh: 當大為申飭。

translations.literal: This should be greatly admonished and rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Both evils demand stern correction.

sentences.zh: 」因條八式以獻。

translations.literal: "He thereupon submitted eight formulae for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: "He then offered eight model regulations.

sentences.zh: 帝即命頒之天下。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered them promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered them promulgated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 給事中汪始亨極論盜屯損餉之弊。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wang Shiheng argued forcefully against the abuse of stolen garrison land harming supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Shiheng attacked at length the drain on rations from encroachment on garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 自嚴言：「相沿已久，難於核實。

translations.literal: Ziyan said: "The practice has long continued and is hard to verify in fact.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan replied: "The practice is ancient and hard to audit.

sentences.zh: 請無論軍種民種，一照民田起科。

translations.literal: I request that regardless of military or civilian tenure, all be assessed alike according to civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: Let every plot, whether held by soldier or commoner, be taxed as ordinary farmland.

sentences.zh: 」帝是其議。

translations.literal: "The emperor approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 先是，忠賢亂政，邊餉多缺，自嚴給發如期。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongxian disturbed government, frontier pay was often short, yet Ziyan disbursed on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Zhongxian's misrule frontier funds had often run dry; Ziyan still paid on time.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「最耗財者無如客餉。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "What most drains treasure is none other than guest rations.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "Nothing bleeds the treasury like guest rations.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮年例合三百二十七萬，而客餉居三之一，宜大裁省。

translations.literal: The annual quotas of the garrisons together total three million twenty-seven thousand, and guest rations occupy one third—they should be greatly cut.
translations.idiomatic: All garrison quotas together come to 3,270,000 taels, and guest rations swallow a third; they must be slashed.

sentences.zh: 其次則有撫賞、召買、修築諸費，皆不可不節。

translations.literal: Next come reward silver, requisitions, and construction costs—all must be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Reward payments, palace purchases, and construction costs come next, and none may be left unchecked.

sentences.zh: 」帝褒納之。

translations.literal: "The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor praised the advice and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 其冬，京師被兵，帝憂勞國事，旨中夜數發。

translations.literal: That winter the capital was threatened by enemy troops; the emperor, worn by state affairs, issued rescripts deep into the night.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the capital came under arms; worn down by the crisis, the emperor sent rescripts deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 自嚴奏答無滯，不敢安寢，頭目臃腫，事幸無乏。

translations.literal: Ziyan answered memorials without delay, not daring to rest; his head and eyes swelled, yet affairs fortunately did not fail for want of him.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan answered every dispatch without delay, scarcely sleeping; his head and eyes swelled with fatigue, yet the supply lines held.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，以六罪自劾，乞罷，優旨慰留。

translations.literal: The next summer he impeached himself on six charges and begged dismissal; a gracious edict comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he submitted six counts against himself and asked to retire; a gracious edict refused and bade him stay.

sentences.zh: 先以考滿加太子少保，敘遵、永克復功，再進太子太保。

translations.literal: Earlier, upon completion of his performance review, he had been given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; for the recovery of Zun and Yong he was advanced again to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent at his review; after the recovery of Zunhua and Yongping he was raised to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書梁廷棟請增天下田賦，自嚴不能止。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liang Tingdong requested increasing the land tax throughout the realm; Ziyan could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Liang Tingdong proposed raising the land tax empire-wide, and Ziyan could not block it.

sentences.zh: 於是舊增五百二十萬之外，更增百六十五萬有奇，天下益耗矣。

translations.literal: Thus beyond the old increase of five million two hundred thousand, another one hundred sixty-five thousand-odd was added, and the realm grew still more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: On top of the earlier increase of 5.2 million taels came another 165,000-odd, and the empire grew poorer still.

sentences.zh: 已，陳時務十事，意主利民，帝悉采納。

translations.literal: Soon he presented ten items on current affairs, their intent chiefly to benefit the people; the emperor adopted them all.
translations.idiomatic: He soon offered ten reforms aimed chiefly at relieving the people, and the emperor adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 又以兵餉日增，屢請清核，而兵部及督撫率為寢閣。

translations.literal: Because military pay rose daily, he repeatedly requested a thorough audit, but the Ministry of War and the supervising grand coordinators generally buried the matter.
translations.idiomatic: As military costs climbed he repeatedly demanded a clean audit, but the Ministry of War and the frontier governors let each request die in committee.

sentences.zh: 復乞汰內地無用之兵，帝即令嚴飭，然不能盡行也。

translations.literal: He again begged to eliminate useless troops in the interior; the emperor at once ordered strict rectification, yet it could not be fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to cut useless interior garrisons; the emperor ordered immediate reform, yet the purge never fully took hold.

sentences.zh: 御史余應桂劾自嚴殿試讀卷，首薦陳於泰，乃輔臣周延儒姻婭。

translations.literal: Censor Yu Yinggui impeached Ziyan for reading examination papers and placing Chen Yutai first—Chen was a relative by marriage of Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yu Yinggui accused Ziyan of ranking Chen Yutai first in the palace examination—Chen was related by marriage to Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru.

sentences.zh: 自嚴引疾乞休，疏四上，不允。

translations.literal: Ziyan cited illness and begged retirement; four memorials went up without approval.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan pleaded illness and asked to retire; four memorials went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 時有詔，縣令將行取者，戶部先核其錢谷。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict that magistrates about to be selected for promotion must first have their grain accounts verified by the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required that any magistrate slated for capital promotion must first have his grain accounts cleared by the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 華亭知縣鄭友元已入為御史，先任青浦，逋金花銀二千九百。

translations.literal: Zheng Youyuan, magistrate of Huating, had already entered service as a censor; he had previously served in Qingpu and was in arrears on golden-flower silver by two thousand nine hundred taels.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Youyuan of Huating had already been made a censor, though his earlier post at Qingpu still owed 2,900 taels in golden-flower silver.

sentences.zh: 帝以詰戶部，自嚴言友元已輸十之七貯太倉。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the Ministry of Revenue; Ziyan said Youyuan had already paid seven-tenths, stored in the Grand Canal granary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demanded an answer from the ministry; Ziyan said Youyuan had already paid seven-tenths into the Grand Canal granary.

sentences.zh: 帝令主庫者核實，無有，帝怒責自嚴。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chief storekeeper to verify; there was nothing, and the emperor angrily rebuked Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the warehouse chief to check; the payment did not exist, and the emperor rebuked Ziyan in fury.

sentences.zh: 自嚴飾詞辨，帝益怒，遂下自嚴獄，遣使逮友元。

translations.literal: Ziyan embellished his words in defense; the emperor grew still angrier and had Ziyan imprisoned and sent envoys to arrest Youyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan tried to talk his way clear; the emperor's rage only deepened, and Ziyan was thrown into prison while agents were sent to seize Youyuan.

sentences.zh: 御史李若讜疏救，不納。

translations.literal: Censor Li Ruoxun memorialized in rescue; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Ruoxun submitted a rescue memorial; it was rejected.

sentences.zh: 逾月，給事中吳甘來復抗疏論救，帝乃釋之。

translations.literal: After more than a month, supervising secretary Wu Ganlai again submitted a defiant memorial pleading for him, and the emperor then released him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later supervising secretary Wu Ganlai risked another blunt plea, and the emperor finally set Ziyan free.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，敘四川平賊功，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year, in recognition of merit in pacifying bandits in Sichuan, his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year, rewarded for pacifying rebels in Sichuan, he was restored to rank and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 又三年卒，賜恤如制。

translations.literal: Three years later he died, and condolence gifts were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died, and the usual posthumous honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 李長庚，字酉卿，麻城人。

translations.literal: Li Zhanggeng, courtesy name Youqing, was a man of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhanggeng, styled Youqing, came from Macheng.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷江西左、右布政使，所在勵清操。

translations.literal: He served as left and right administration commissioner of Jiangxi; wherever he was, he urged pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right administration commissioner in Jiangxi, everywhere urging clean government.

sentences.zh: 入為順天府尹。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to the capital as prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 改右副都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 盡心荒政，民賴以蘇。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to famine relief, and the people relied on him to recover.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into famine relief, and the people lived again because of him.

sentences.zh: 盜蔓武定諸州縣，討擒其渠魁。

translations.literal: Bandits spread through the prefectures and counties of Wuding; he campaigned and captured their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry engulfed Wuding and neighboring counties, he marched out and seized the chiefs.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，遼東用兵，議行登、萊海運。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, when troops were used in Liaodong, it was debated to run sea transport from Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year, as Liaodong mobilized for war, the court debated sea transport from Dengzhou and Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 長庚初言不便，後言：「自登州望鐵山西北口，至羊頭凹，歷中島、長行島抵北信口，又歷兔兒島至深井，達蓋州，剝運一百二十里，抵娘娘宮，陸行至廣寧一百八十里，至遼陽一百六十里，每石費一金。

translations.literal: Zhanggeng at first said it was inconvenient; later he said: "From Dengzhou one looks toward the northwest mouth of Tieshan, to Yangtou'ao, passing Central Island and Changxing Island to reach Beixin Mouth, then passing Rabbit Island to Shenjing, reaching Gaizhou; transshipment one hundred twenty li, reaching Niangniang Palace; overland one hundred eighty li to Guangning, one hundred sixty li to Liaoyang—each shi costs one tael of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanggeng first called the route impractical; later he wrote: "From Dengzhou, sighting the northwest mouth of Tieshan to Yangtou'ao, past Central Island and Longxing Island to Beixin Mouth, then past Rabbit Island to Deep Well and on to Gaizhou, transshipment runs 120 li to Niangniang Palace; overland it is 180 li to Guangning and 160 li to Liaoyang—one tael of silver per shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 」部議以為便，遂行之。

translations.literal: "The ministry debated and deemed it convenient, and it was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: "The ministry judged the plan workable, and the route was opened.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，特設戶部侍郎一人兼右僉都御史，出督遼餉，駐天津，即以長庚為之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially appointed, also holding Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to go out and supervise Liaodong provisions, stationed at Tianjin—and Zhanggeng was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, a Vice Minister of Revenue was created, concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to supervise Liaodong supplies from Tianjin, and Zhanggeng received the post.

sentences.zh: 奏行造淮船、通津路、議牛車、酌海道、截幫運、議錢法、設按臣、開事例、嚴海防九事。

translations.literal: He memorialized implementation of nine measures: building Huai River ships, opening ferry roads, debating ox carts, weighing the sea route, cutting convoy transport, debating currency, appointing investigating commissioners, opening precedent purchases, and tightening coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed nine reforms—build Huai River barges, open ferry routes, organize ox carts, chart the sea lane, trim convoy transport, reform the currency, appoint investigating commissioners, authorize precedent purchases, and tighten coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 時議歲運米百八十萬石，豆九十萬石，草二千一百六十萬束，銀三百二十四萬兩，長庚請留金花，行改折，借稅課，言：「臣考會計錄，每歲本色、折色通計千四百六十一萬有奇。

translations.literal: At the time it was debated to transport annually 1.8 million shi of rice, 900,000 shi of beans, 21.6 million bundles of fodder, and 3.24 million taels of silver; Zhanggeng requested retaining golden-flower silver, carrying out conversion to silver payments, and borrowing tax levies, saying: "Your servant has examined the accounting records: each year in kind and commuted payments together total 14,610,000-odd.
translations.idiomatic: The annual plan called for 1.8 million shi of rice, 900,000 shi of beans, 21.6 million bundles of fodder, and 3.24 million taels of silver; Zhanggeng asked to retain golden-flower payments, commute more dues to silver, and borrow tax revenues, writing: "I have reviewed the accounts: in kind and commuted payments together exceed 14,610,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 入內府者六百余萬，入太倉者，自本色外，折色四百余萬。

translations.literal: What enters the inner palace is more than six million; what enters the Grand Canal granary, apart from payments in kind, is more than four million in commuted payments.
translations.idiomatic: More than six million flows to the inner palace; to the Grand Canal granary, beyond payments in kind, another four million-odd in commuted silver.

sentences.zh: 內府六百萬，自金花籽粒外，皆絲綿布帛蠟茶顏料之類，歲久皆朽敗。

translations.literal: The inner palace's six million, apart from golden-flower grain, is all silk, cotton, cloth, wax, tea, pigments, and the like—over the years all rot away.
translations.idiomatic: Of the six million for the inner palace, everything beyond golden-flower grain is silk, cotton, wax, tea, dyes, and the like—year after year it rots unused.

sentences.zh: 若改折一年，無損於上，有益於下。

translations.literal: If commuted for one year, there would be no harm above and benefit below.
translations.idiomatic: Commute it for one year and the throne loses nothing while the realm gains.

sentences.zh: 他若陜西羊絨，江、浙織造，亦當稍停一年，濟軍國急。

translations.literal: Likewise Shaanxi sheep fleece and Jiang-Zhe weaving should also be suspended a year to relieve the army and state in their urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise Shaanxi fleece levies and Jiang-Zhe weaving ought to pause for a year to meet the army's urgent need.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，言：「金花籽粒本祖宗舊制，內供正額及軍官月俸，所費不貲，安得借留？

translations.literal: "The emperor was displeased and said, "Golden-flower grain is the ancestral institution; the regular inner supply and officers' monthly salaries cost beyond reckoning—how can it be borrowed and retained?"
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor took offense and said, "Golden-flower grain is an ancestral institution; the regular inner supply and officers' monthly pay cost sums beyond counting—how dare you propose to retain it?"

sentences.zh: 其以今年天津、通州、江西、四川、廣西上供稅銀，盡充軍費。

translations.literal: Let the tribute tax silver submitted this year from Tianjin, Tongzhou, Jiangxi, Sichuan, and Guangxi fully supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Let this year's tribute silver from Tianjin, Tongzhou, Jiangxi, Sichuan, and Guangxi be applied entirely to military expenses.

sentences.zh: 」於是戶科給事中官應震上言：「考《會典》，於內庫則云：金花銀，國初解南京供武俸，諸邊或有急，亦取給其中。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Guan Yingzhen, supervising secretary of the Revenue Section, submitted a memorial: "Consulting the *Collected Statutes*, regarding the inner treasury it states: golden-flower silver—in the founding era was delivered to Nanjing to supply military salaries; when any frontier had an emergency, funds could also be drawn from it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Revenue Section supervising secretary Guan Yingzhen then memorialized: "According to the *Collected Statutes*, the inner treasury entry reads that golden-flower silver was first sent to Nanjing for military pay, and when a frontier was hard pressed, the same funds could be drawn upon.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，始自南京改解內庫。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Zhengtong reign it began to be redirected from Nanjing and delivered to the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 it was first redirected from Nanjing to the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 嗣後除武官俸外，皆為禦用。

translations.literal: Thereafter, apart from military officers' salaries, all was for the sovereign's use.
translations.idiomatic: After that, save for officers' pay, everything went to the imperial privy purse.

sentences.zh: 是金花銀國初常以濟邊，而正統後方供禦用也。

translations.literal: Thus golden-flower silver in the founding era was constantly used to relieve the frontiers, and only after Zhengtong did it supply the sovereign's use.
translations.idiomatic: So golden-flower silver originally eased the frontiers; only after Zhengtong did it feed the privy purse.

sentences.zh: 《會典》於太倉庫則云：嘉靖二十二年，題準諸處京運錢糧，不拘金花籽粒，應解內府者悉解貯太倉庫，備各邊應用。

translations.literal: The *Collected Statutes* regarding the Grand Canal granary states: in the twenty-second year of Jiajing it was approved that grain and funds transported to the capital from all regions, whether golden-flower or grain dues, all that should have gone to the inner palace were to be delivered and stored in the Grand Canal granary, to supply each frontier as needed.
translations.idiomatic: On the Grand Canal granary, the *Collected Statutes* record that in Jiajing 22 capital-transport grain and silver—golden-flower or otherwise—that would have gone to the inner palace was ordered stored at the Grand Canal granary for frontier use.

sentences.zh: 是世宗朝金花盡充兵餉，不知陛下初年何故斂之於內也。

translations.literal: Thus in the Shizong reign golden-flower fully supplied military rations; one does not know why in Your Majesty's early years it was gathered inward.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong, golden-flower silver fed the armies entirely—why Your Majesty's early reign drew it back inward is unclear.

sentences.zh: 今不考各邊取給應用之例，而反雲正供舊額，何相左若是？

translations.literal: Now without examining the precedents by which the frontiers drew and applied funds, yet instead saying it is the old quota of regular supply—how can they be so opposed?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty cites the old regular quota without the frontier precedents for drawing supplies—how can the two accounts square?

sentences.zh: 至武官月俸，歲不過十余萬，乃雲所費不貲哉。

translations.literal: As for military officers' monthly salaries, in a year they do not exceed a little over one hundred thousand—yet you say the expense is beyond reckoning?
translations.idiomatic: Officers' monthly pay never exceeds a hundred thousand taels a year—how can it be called beyond reckoning?

sentences.zh: 且原數一百萬，陛下始增二十萬，年深日久，顛末都忘。

translations.literal: Moreover the original sum was one million; Your Majesty first added two hundred thousand; years deep and time long, the beginning and end are all forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: The original figure was one million taels; Your Majesty added two hundred thousand; in the passing years the whole story has been forgotten.

sentences.zh: 以臣計之，毋論今年當借，即嗣後年年借用可也；

translations.literal: By your servant's reckoning, whether this year it should be borrowed, or hereafter year after year it may be borrowed;
translations.idiomatic: In my reckoning, this year may borrow it, and in years to come it may be borrowed every year;

sentences.zh: 毋論未來者當濟邊，即見在內帑者盡還太倉可也。

translations.literal: whether what is to come should relieve the frontiers, or what is now in the inner treasury should all be returned to the Grand Canal granary—that too may be done.
translations.idiomatic: future revenue may ease the frontiers, and what already sits in the inner treasury may all be returned to the Grand Canal granary.

sentences.zh: 若夫物料改折，隆慶元年曾行之以解部濟邊，六年又行於南京監局，亦以濟邊。

translations.literal: As for converting material levies to silver payments, in the first year of Longqing it was once carried out to relieve the ministry and ease the frontiers; in the sixth year it was again carried out at the Nanjing supervisory bureaus, likewise to ease the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: Commuting material levies to silver was tried in Longqing 1 to fund the ministry and the frontiers, and again in Longqing 6 at the Nanjing supervisory bureaus for the same purpose.

sentences.zh: 此則祖宗舊制，陛下獨不聞耶？

translations.literal: These are the ancestral institutions—has Your Majesty alone not heard?
translations.idiomatic: These are ancestral precedents—has Your Majesty not heard of them?

sentences.zh: 」帝卒不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor in the end would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 時諸事創始，百務坌集，長庚悉辦治。

translations.literal: At the time many matters were being launched anew and a hundred affairs thronged together; Zhanggeng managed them all.
translations.idiomatic: With every office launching new undertakings at once, Zhanggeng handled the full crush of business.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，遷南京刑部尚書，就移戶部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was transferred to Minister of Justice at Nanjing, and then moved to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he became Nanjing Minister of Justice, then moved to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜戶部尚書，未任，以憂歸。

translations.literal: The following year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue; before he took office he returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned as Minister of Revenue but went home in mourning before assuming the post.

sentences.zh: 誌道，漳浦人，天啟時為給事中。

translations.literal: Zhidao, a man of Zhangpu, was a supervising secretary in the Tianqi era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidao of Zhangpu served as a supervising secretary under Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 議「三案」為高攀龍所駁，謝病歸。

translations.literal: When he deliberated on the "Three Cases" he was rebutted by Gao Panlong and withdrew on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: His argument on the "Three Cases" was refuted by Gao Panlong, and he resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 其後附魏忠賢，歷擢左通政，論者薄之。

translations.literal: Later he attached himself to Wei Zhongxian and was promoted in succession to Left Commissioner of the Transmission Office; commentators despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He later sided with Wei Zhongxian and rose to Left Commissioner of the Transmission Office, for which critics held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 及是，以忤中官罷。

translations.literal: At this juncture he was dismissed for offending an inner eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he was dismissed for crossing an inner eunuch.

sentences.zh: 長庚不植黨援，與溫體仁不甚合。

translations.literal: Zhanggeng did not cultivate factional backing and was not altogether in accord with Wen Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanggeng kept no factional ties and got on poorly with Wen Tiren.

sentences.zh: 推郎中王茂學為真定知府，帝不允。

translations.literal: He recommended the bureau director Wang Maoxue for prefect of Zhending; the emperor did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended bureau director Wang Maoxue for Zhending prefect, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 復推為順德知府，帝怒，責以欺蒙，並追咎冠帶監生授職事，責令回奏。

translations.literal: He recommended him again for prefect of Shunde; the emperor was angry and rebuked him for deceit, also pursuing blame for the matter of conferring office on imperial students with honorary rank, and ordered him to return with a memorial in reply.
translations.idiomatic: A second recommendation for Shunde prefect enraged the emperor, who accused him of deception, also revisiting appointments granted to honorary students with rank, and demanded a written reply.

sentences.zh: 奏上，斥為民。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted he was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: His reply brought dismissal to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，國變，久之卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home ten years; the realm changed; after long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement ten years, survived the dynastic collapse, and died not long after.

sentences.zh: 劉之鳳，字雍鳴，中牟人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhifeng, style name Yongming, was a man of Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhifeng, styled Yongming, was from Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Wanli 44.

sentences.zh: 歷南京御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts as a Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年六月，上疏別白孫承宗、王象乾、閻鳴泰本末，請定去留，而撤毛文龍海外軍，令居關內。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Tianqi he submitted a memorial clarifying the full stories of Sun Chengzong, Wang Xiangqian, and Yan Mingtai, asking to fix who should remain or go, while withdrawing Mao Wenlong's overseas army and ordering it to reside within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 3, sixth month, he memorialized to sort out the cases of Sun Chengzong, Wang Xiangqian, and Yan Mingtai, settle their appointments, withdraw Mao Wenlong's force beyond the sea, and station it inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 又請亟罷內操。

translations.literal: He also asked urgently to abolish the inner training corps.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the immediate abolition of the palace guard drill corps.

sentences.zh: 忤魏忠賢，傳旨切責，復宣諭廷臣，再瀆奏者罪無赦。

translations.literal: Offending Wei Zhongxian, an edict in the emperor's name sternly rebuked him and again proclaimed to the court officials that whoever again submitted impertinent memorials would not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Wei Zhongxian and received a stern rescript; the throne further warned the court that repeat offenders would not be spared.

sentences.zh: 六年，之鳳方視江防，期滿奏報。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zhifeng was inspecting river defenses; when his term ended he submitted his report.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, while inspecting river defenses, he filed his term-end report.

sentences.zh: 忠賢奪其職。

translations.literal: Zhongxian stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，起故官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 帝召周延儒燕見，宵分始出。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Zhou Yanru for a banquet audience; only at deep night did he leave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhou Yanru to a private banquet that lasted until midnight.

sentences.zh: 之鳳偕同官上疏曰：「臣等待罪陪京，去延儒原籍三百里，其立身居鄉，不堪置齒頰。

translations.literal: Zhifeng together with his colleagues submitted a memorial saying: "We your servants await punishment while serving in the southern capital; three hundred li from Yanru's native place, his conduct in office and in the village is not fit to be mentioned between teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng and his colleagues memorialized: "We await punishment in the southern capital, yet lie three hundred li from Yanru's home district and know his conduct in office and at home is not fit to be named.

sentences.zh: 今乃特蒙眷註，必將曰舉朝盡欺，獨延儒一人捐軀為國，使陛下真若廷臣無可信，而延儒乃得翦所忌，樹所私，曰為馮銓、霍維華等報怨。

translations.literal: Now he alone receives special favor—people will surely say that the whole court deceives you and Yanru alone offers his person for the state, making Your Majesty truly as if no courtier can be trusted, while Yanru can cut down those he hates, raise those he favors, claiming to avenge Feng Quan, Huo Weihua, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: This special favor will be read as proof that every minister deceives you and Yanru alone sacrifices himself for the realm—as if none of us were trustworthy—while he cuts down his enemies, raises his clients, and calls it vengeance for Feng Quan and Huo Weihua.

sentences.zh: 此一召也，於國事無纖毫益，而於聖德有丘山之損。

translations.literal: This single summons brings no thread or hair of benefit to state affairs, yet to sagely virtue a loss like mountains and hills.
translations.idiomatic: One such summons aids state affairs not in the least while it mars imperial virtue as a mountain might be marred.

sentences.zh: 」忤旨，詰責。

translations.literal: " Offending the imperial will, he was interrogated and rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: " The rescript rebuked him harshly.

sentences.zh: 已，復列上五事，曰舉謀勇，止援兵，練土著，密偵探，選守令，俱見采納。

translations.literal: Later he again listed five measures: promote strategists and the brave; halt relief troops; drill local natives; tighten espionage; select prefects and magistrates—all were adopted.
