translations.idiomatic: He later offered five programs—promote stratagems and valor, stop relief armies, drill local troops, tighten intelligence, and pick prefects and magistrates—and all were accepted.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部侍郎，遂代鄭三俊為本部尚書。

translations.literal: Promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Justice, he then replaced Zheng Sanjun as Minister of that department.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Justice and then succeeded Zheng Sanjun as Minister.

sentences.zh: 之鳳以天下囚徒皆五年一審錄，高墻罪獨不與，上疏言之，報可。

translations.literal: Zhifeng, because all prisoners in the realm undergo case review every five years while those guilty of high-wall offenses alone do not participate, submitted a memorial on it and received approval.
translations.idiomatic: Noting that all prisoners undergo quinquennial review except those held on high-wall offenses, he memorialized for their inclusion and won approval.

sentences.zh: 嘗與左侍郎王命璿召對平臺，論律例及獄情，帝申飭而退。

translations.literal: He once was summoned with Left Vice Minister Wang Mingsuan to audience at the Flat Terrace, discussing statutes and prison cases; the emperor sternly admonished and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned with Left Vice Minister Wang Mingsuan to the Flat Terrace to discuss statutes and cases, he met stern admonition and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 時有火星之變，之鳳特請修刑，言：「自今獄情大者，一月奏斷，小者半月。

translations.literal: At the time there was a Martian anomaly; Zhifeng especially asked to reform punishment, saying: "From now on, major prison cases shall be reported and decided within one month, minor ones within half a month.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars wandered off course, he urged penal reform: "Major cases should be decided within a month hereafter, minor ones within half a month.

sentences.zh: 贓重人犯，結案在數年前者，大抵本犯無髓可敲，戚屬亦無脂可吸。

translations.literal: Heavy corruption convicts whose cases were concluded several years ago—for the most part the principal offender has no marrow left to be squeezed out, and kinsmen have no fat to be sucked.
translations.idiomatic: For grave corruption cases settled years ago, the principal offender has no marrow left to squeeze and kin no fat to wring out.

sentences.zh: 祈悉宥免，全好生之仁。

translations.literal: I pray that all be wholly pardoned, completing the benevolence of sparing life.
translations.idiomatic: I beg complete pardon for them all, in keeping with the virtue of sparing life.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 然之鳳雖為此奏，其後每上獄詞，帝必嚴駁，之鳳懼甚，諸司呈稿，遲疑不敢遽發，屢疏謝病，帝不從。

translations.literal: Yet although Zhifeng made this memorial, afterward whenever he submitted prison case reports the emperor would sternly reject them; Zhifeng was greatly afraid; when the various offices presented drafts he hesitated and did not dare quickly issue them; repeatedly he memorialized asking leave on illness, and the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after this memorial every case report he sent up met stern rejection; Zhifeng grew fearful, dared not promptly issue drafts from the offices, and repeatedly begged sick leave without success.

sentences.zh: 會尚書範景文劾南京給事中荊可棟貪墨，下部訊，之鳳予輕比。

translations.literal: It happened that Minister Fan Jingwen impeached Nanjing supervising secretary Jing Kedong for corruption; the case was sent down for interrogation, and Zhifeng applied a light statute of comparison.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Fan Jingwen impeached Nanjing supervising secretary Jing Kedong for graft and the case went to trial, Zhifeng matched it to a lighter statute.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其受賄，下之吏，法司希旨坐絞。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected he had taken bribes, sent him down to the judicial officers, and the law officers to please the will sentenced him to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting bribery, the emperor handed him to the judicial authorities, who to please the throne sentenced him to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 給事中李清言於律未合，同官葛樞復論救。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Li Qing said it did not accord with the law; colleague Ge Shu again memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Li Qing argued the sentence did not fit the law; colleague Ge Shu memorialized again in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，鐫樞級，調外。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, reduced Shu's rank by inscription, and transferred him outside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck Ge Shu from rank and transferred him outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，之鳳獄中上書自白無贓賄，情可矜原。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year Zhifeng from prison submitted a memorial whitewashing himself, that there was no bribery and the circumstances merited pity and restoration.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Chongzhen 13 he wrote from prison that he had taken no bribe and deserved mercy.

sentences.zh: 亦置不省，竟瘐死。

translations.literal: It too was set aside unheeded; in the end he died of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The plea went unheeded and he wasted away in prison.

sentences.zh: 計崇禎朝刑部易尚書十七人。

translations.literal: It is reckoned that in the Chongzhen reign the Ministry of Justice changed ministers seventeen times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen the Ministry of Justice saw seventeen ministers.

sentences.zh: 薛貞以奄黨抵死。

translations.literal: Xue Zhen died at the hands of the eunuch faction.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhen died for his ties to the eunuch faction.

sentences.zh: 蘇茂相半歲而罷。

translations.literal: Su Maoxiang was dismissed within half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Su Maoxiang lasted half a year and left office.

sentences.zh: 王在晉未任，改兵部。

translations.literal: Wang Zaijin, before assuming office, was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zaijin was shifted to War before he took up the post.

sentences.zh: 喬允升坐逸囚遣戍。

translations.literal: Qiao Yunsheng was banished for allowing a prisoner to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yunsheng was exiled for letting a prisoner escape.

sentences.zh: 韓繼思坐議獄除名。

translations.literal: Han Jisi was removed from the rolls for deliberating on a prison case.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jisi was struck from the rolls over a prison deliberation.

sentences.zh: 胡應臺獨得善去。

translations.literal: Hu Yingtai alone secured a favorable departure.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yingtai alone left office honorably.

sentences.zh: 馮英被劾遣戍。

translations.literal: Feng Ying was impeached and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ying was impeached and exiled.

sentences.zh: 鄭三俊坐議獄逮系。

translations.literal: Zheng Sanjun was arrested for deliberating on a prison case.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun was arrested over a prison case.

sentences.zh: 之鳳論絞，瘐死獄中。

translations.literal: Zhifeng was sentenced to strangulation and died of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng was sentenced to strangulation and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 甄淑坐納賄下詔獄，改系刑部，瘐死。

translations.literal: Zhen Shu was imprisoned in the edict prison for taking bribes, then transferred to the Ministry of Justice and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Shu entered the edict prison for bribery, was moved to Justice, and died there.

sentences.zh: 李覺斯坐議獄削籍。

translations.literal: Li Juesi was struck from the rolls for deliberating on a prison case.
translations.idiomatic: Li Juesi was struck from the rolls over a prison case.

sentences.zh: 劉澤深卒於位。

translations.literal: Liu Zeshen died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zeshen died in post.

sentences.zh: 鄭三俊再為尚書，改吏部。

translations.literal: Zheng Sanjun again became Minister and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun became Minister again, then moved to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 範景文未任，改工部。

translations.literal: Fan Jingwen, before assuming office, was transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jingwen was shifted to Works before taking office.

sentences.zh: 徐石麒坐議獄，落職閑住。

translations.literal: Xu Shiqin was dismissed from office for deliberating on a prison case and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiqin lost his post over a prison deliberation and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 胡應臺再召不赴。

translations.literal: Hu Yingtai was summoned again but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yingtai was recalled but declined to return.

sentences.zh: 繼其後者張忻，賊陷京師，與子庶吉士端並降。

translations.literal: The one who followed him was Zhang Xin; when bandits took the capital he and his son, a Hanlin bachelor named Duan, both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: His successor Zhang Xin, when rebels took the capital, surrendered together with his son Duan, a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：崔景榮、黃克纘皆不為東林所與，然特不附東林耳。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Cui Jingrong and Huang Kezuan were both not given by the Donglin, yet they simply did not attach to the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Cui Jingrong and Huang Kezuan were no friends of the Donglin, yet they merely refused to join it.

sentences.zh: 方東林勢盛，羅天下清流，士有落然自異者，詬誶隨之矣。

translations.literal: When the Donglin's power was flourishing it gathered the pure streams of the realm; if a gentleman stood apart, abuse followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Donglin dominated it gathered the realm's upright men; anyone who stood apart invited abuse.

sentences.zh: 攻東林者，幸其近己也，而援以為重。

translations.literal: Those who attacked the Donglin rejoiced that such men were near themselves and took them as weight.
translations.idiomatic: Its enemies welcomed allies near at hand and treated them as weighty supporters.

sentences.zh: 於是中立者類不免蒙小人之玷。

translations.literal: Thus the neutral sort mostly could not avoid being stained by petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Neutrals therefore often shared the petty men's stain.

sentences.zh: 核人品者，乃專以與東林厚薄為輕重，豈篤論哉？

translations.literal: Those who gauged persons' quality took thickness or thinness with the Donglin as light or heavy—was that a solid judgment?
translations.idiomatic: Yet judges of character weighed men only by their distance from the Donglin—is that sound judgment?

sentences.zh: 畢自嚴、李長庚計臣中辦治才，而自嚴增賦之議，識者病焉。

translations.literal: Bi Ziyan and Li Zhanggeng were talents for handling affairs among revenue officials; yet Ziyan's proposal to increase levies, discerning persons faulted.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Ziyan and Li Zhanggeng were capable revenue ministers, though critics condemned Ziyan's tax increase.

sentences.zh: 劉之鳳議獄不當，罪止謫罷，竟予重比，刑罰不中，欲求治得乎！

translations.literal: Liu Zhifeng's improper prison deliberation deserved only demotion and dismissal, yet he was given a heavy comparison; punishments did not hit the mark—can good governance be sought?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhifeng misjudged a case that warranted demotion at most, yet received strangulation; when punishment misses its mark, how can order be achieved?
